questions.prompt: Why have you chosen this university and this course over the others you applied to?
questions.hint: Name the modules and what they lead to. 'It was the offer I got' is the answer that fails this.

questions.prompt: How will you pay your tuition and living costs, and where is that money now?
questions.hint: Name the sponsor, their relationship to you, and the account the funds have been held in.

questions.prompt: What do you know about the modules in your first year?
questions.hint: Two or three by name, and what each one covers. Read the course page before this interview.

questions.prompt: What do you plan to do after you graduate?
questions.hint: A specific role and where — the Graduate Route or a plan back home both answer this well.

questions.prompt: Why do you want to study in the UK rather than in your own country?
questions.hint: Give a reason about the course and the sector, not about immigration.

questions.prompt: Tell me about your course. How long is it, what will you study, and how much does it cost?
questions.hint: Know the duration, the tuition figure and two or three modules. Vagueness here is what refusals cite.

questions.prompt: Where will you live, and how much will it cost you each month?
questions.hint: A city, a rough rent, and how it fits the maintenance funds you have shown.

questions.prompt: What will you do when your visa ends?
questions.hint: Answer plainly. A clear plan reads as genuine; a vague one reads as an intention to stay.

questions.prompt: Why this programme, and how does it follow on from what you have already studied?
questions.hint: Name two modules and link them to a project or a paper you have actually worked on.

questions.prompt: Talk me through a piece of work you led. What went wrong, and what did you do about it?
questions.hint: Situation, action, result — and give the result a number.

questions.prompt: Whose research in the department interests you, and why?
questions.hint: Reference the work, not just the name. A paper or a lab, and what you found interesting in it.

questions.prompt: What would you want to be doing five years after you graduate?
questions.hint: Tie it back to what this programme actually teaches.
